subject: English Language

questions.prompt: How many children did Mtokambali have? (a 2, b 3, c 4, d 5, e 6)
steps: The page 4 listening script states two children.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: How many people made up his family? (a 4, b 5, c 6, d 3, e 2)
steps: Count Mtokambali, his wife and two children: 1 + 1 + 2 = 4.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: How old was the first-born child? (a 3, b 6, c 9, d 4, e 5)
steps: The script gives the first child's age.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What fuel did they use to start the fire? (a kerosene, b firewood, c jerry, d petrol, e diesel)
steps: The script distinguishes ignition kerosene from cooking wood/charcoal.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What does prohibit mean? (a forbid, b allow, c break, d prevent, e surpass)
steps: The mother forbids touching matches or making fire.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Pupils used to ___ a song at break. (a singing, b sung, c sang, d sing, e sings)
steps: Used to takes the base verb.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: We have been ___ here since 1990. (a lived, b live, c living, d will live, e lives)
steps: Have been plus ing forms present perfect continuous.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Jackson ___ prizes last year. (a gets, b getting, c did get, d has gotten, e got)
steps: Last year requires past tense.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: e. Got is the usual answer; c. did get is grammatical emphasis.

questions.prompt: The dog is healthy because it ___ good food. (a eat, b eats, c eating, d eaten, e is eat)
steps: It takes eats for a present habit.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Jessica ___ bananas every day. (a pick, b picks, c is picking, d will pick, e picking)
steps: A singular habitual subject takes picks; the later source sell should likewise be sells.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: ___ you coming to the match? Bank: will elect, shall, fell, the, some, neither, if, since, to.
steps: The present continuous question is Are you coming?
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Are is required but absent from the bank.

questions.prompt: They ___ a school government next Sunday.
steps: The future verb phrase matches next Sunday.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Their father ___ asleep after dinner.
steps: Fell asleep is the correct past phrase.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Our teacher has worked at this school ___.
steps: The question ends after the blank, so since alone cannot supply the missing time information.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Incomplete item: since requires a starting time; for requires a duration. Example only: since 2020.

questions.prompt: Would you prefer tea ___ coffee?
steps: Prefer X to Y compares preferences; the bank gives to.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: To (intended comparison). Natural alternative-choice question: Would you prefer tea or coffee?

questions.prompt: Match abroad: A cemetery, B butchery, C outside, D equipment, E exile, F grave, G niece.
steps: Abroad is more specific than just outside a building.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. Outside is the closest bank choice; precise meaning: in another country/outside one's country.

questions.prompt: Match the plural form of equipment.
steps: Equipment is uncountable; use pieces of equipment for counting.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match the place selling meat.
steps: A butchery sells meat.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match your sister's daughter.
steps: Niece is the female child of a sibling.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match a place where many dead people are buried.
steps: A cemetery contains many graves.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order A-E: The dog asked the cat to sleep near the door.
steps: The plan follows introduction and the unattended meat.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: When the cat slept, the dog ate the meat.
steps: The theft follows the trick.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Mrs. Peter put meat in the cupboard and went out.
steps: This sets up the opportunity after introducing the animals.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: A dog and cat lived with Mrs. Peter.
steps: Introduce the characters first.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Mrs. Peter returned and found no meat.
steps: Discovery concludes the story.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What is a person who translates English called?
steps: Translator is the general term; interpreter specifies oral interpreting.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A translator; an interpreter if translating spoken language in real time.

questions.prompt: Give a word sounding the same as male (source calls it a homonym).
steps: Male and mail are homophones, with different spellings and meanings.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What is your father's brother called?
steps: A parent's brother is an uncle.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What is an evening meal called?
steps: Both can name the evening meal.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Maize, millet and wheat are examples of what?
steps: All are cereal crops.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Who opened the church door?
steps: The first sentence names him.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Who stole money from the old man?
steps: James accuses Miriam and Father Gashle returns the money she took.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Who brought the money to church?
steps: James brings the bag to Father Gashle.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Who is a thief in the story?
steps: Distinguish the priest's judgement from James's own admission.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Miriam is the person Father Gashle calls the thief. James also admits stealing her bag/money before returning it.

questions.prompt: Who is the old man to Jenny?
steps: The passage calls him Jenny's uncle.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

summaries.Listening: Listen to the supplied teacher text and identify the exact detail asked for. Check spelling and sentence punctuation; missing scripts are explicitly identified.
summaries.Grammar and composition: Follow a clear sequence and keep the tense consistent. Introduce people and events before their pronouns, actions and final outcome.
summaries.Vocabulary and comprehension: Find evidence in the passage or poem before answering. Distinguish explicit statements, reasonable inferences and model interpretations.

references.title: MESP Tanzania Standard Six Terminal Exams May 2024

limitations: 3(i): Required Are is missing from the word bank.
3(iv): The question is truncated before any starting time/duration.
7(iv): Story calls Miriam the thief despite James also admitting theft; both facts are preserved.
